note: From the Conway Parks and Recreation Department's own pages (conwaynh.myrec.com), the Town of Conway website and town code, NH State Parks pages and the Conway Daily Sun, with a source on every item. North Conway is a village inside the Town of Conway, so town parks serve all of Conway. State parks and the private North Conway Community Center are labeled as not town-run.

department.name: Town of Conway Parks and Recreation Department
department.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
department.what: Runs town parks, beaches, ballfields and the Conway Rec Facility (Marshall Gymnasium and the Chip Kennett Teen Center), youth and adult programs, the summer recreation parking permit program and the Schouler Park winter skating rink. The department lists no general email; it asks people to call the main office.

registration.label: Register for programs (MyRec)
registration.note: Create a household account to register for programs. Office visitors should park behind Conway Elementary, not in the SAU 9 or Conway Elementary visitor spaces.

facilities.name: Whitaker Woods and Whitaker Homesite

features: Ball field (baseball diamond) and open field
Trails and open space
Warming house with bathrooms
Cross-country ski trails; passes, info and trail updates through Mount Washington Valley Ski Touring
facilities.seasonal: The Homesite building is listed as closed on the department's facility list. Ski trail updates come from Mount Washington Valley Ski Touring.
facilities.note: Town conservation land. Uses (ball field, trails, open space, warming house) from the town's Conservation, Parks and Recreation Areas page. A Whitaker Woods trail map (2017) is posted on the town Documents page.

facilities.name: Conway public dog park (Thom Steele Way)
facilities.address: 102 Thom Steele Way, Conway, NH (near the Conway Area Humane Society)
features: Separate fenced areas for small dogs (about 5,000 sq ft) and large dogs (about 84,000 sq ft)
ADA-accessible pathways and two accessible parking spaces
Benches, shaded seating and picnic tables
facilities.seasonal: Not open in winter; the site is next to a town snow disposal area.
facilities.note: Town-owned land; resident Tim Quint led the project with donations and grants, and Parks and Rec staff are expected to maintain the grounds in warmer months. Selectmen approved the plans unanimously after a public hearing (Conway Daily Sun, June 24, 2026). The Daily Sun later ran the headline "Blue skies and wagging tails at dog park opening"; that article was not opened.

facilities.name: Echo Lake State Park (NH State Parks, not town)
facilities.address: 68 Echo Lake Road, North Conway, NH 03860
features: Swimming beach and picnic areas
Trail around the lake and trails up to Cathedral Ledge
Fishing, canoeing, mountain biking, snowshoeing
Day use $4 adults, $2 ages 6 to 11; free for 65 and over and 5 and under
facilities.hours: Always open for recreation unless closed or posted
facilities.seasonal: Beach and hiking are unstaffed after October 31; off-season there are no comfort stations and gates may be closed. Pay at the self-serve Iron Ranger station when unstaffed. Pets are not allowed at Echo Lake from May 1 to October 31.
facilities.note: Run by the State of New Hampshire. Park office 603-356-2672.

source.label: NH State Parks, Echo Lake State Park

facilities.name: Cathedral Ledge State Park (NH State Parks, not town)
facilities.address: 579 Cathedral Ledge Road, Bartlett, NH 03812 (address as listed by NH State Parks)
features: 700-foot ledge with a mile-long auto road to the top and views across the Saco River Valley
Scenic overlook, picnic area and a new accessible trail to a valley view
Rock and ice climbing on Cathedral and nearby White Horse ledges
facilities.hours: Always open for recreation unless closed or posted
facilities.seasonal: The park opened for the season May 2 and becomes unstaffed October 31; pay at Iron Ranger stations along the road or at the summit when unstaffed.
facilities.note: Run by the State of New Hampshire. Pets allowed only on hiking trails in the Cathedral and White Horse areas. Carry in, carry out; no drones.

source.label: NH State Parks, Cathedral Ledge State Park

projects.title: Public dog park on Thom Steele Way
projects.summary: A fenced dog park on town land at 102 Thom Steele Way, led by resident Tim Quint and paid for with donations and grants. Selectmen approved the layout unanimously after a June 2026 public hearing. A Conway Daily Sun headline later reported the park's opening.
projects.cost: $62,000 estimate on the town's project page, financed without taxpayer money

source.label: Town of Conway, Proposed Public Dog Park Project

projects.title: Recreation path Phase 2 (Cranmore to Intervale)
projects.summary: Phase 2 would run from the Cranmore trailhead along the north edge of Whitaker Woods and the Mountain Division rail line to Intervale Cross Road. In November 2025 the estimate rose to about $5.6 million and selectmen voted 5-0 not to sign an amended federal EDA grant application, putting the project on hold. The Daily Sun later reported a related warrant article (Article 46) on the April 14 town ballot; its outcome was not verified.
projects.cost: About $5.6 million (up from about $3.3 million), November 2025

source.label: Conway Daily Sun (via Laconia Daily Sun), Nov 28, 2025

projects.title: North Conway Community Center playground renovation (private nonprofit)
projects.summary: The nonprofit community center is rebuilding its playground as a multigenerational space with an ADA-accessible surface and sensory-friendly equipment. Donations of $100 or more are recognized on an indoor plaque.

seasonal.title: Echo Lake and Cathedral Ledge state parks go unstaffed
seasonal.detail: After October 31 both NH State Parks are unstaffed: no comfort stations, gates may be closed, and you pay at self-serve Iron Ranger stations. The parks stay open for recreation unless posted.

source.label: NH State Parks, Echo Lake State Park

seasonal.title: Schouler Park skating rink in winter
seasonal.detail: The outdoor rink at Schouler Park in North Conway Village is open to the public in the winter months; hours depend on weather and ice.

seasonal.title: Dog park closed for winter
seasonal.detail: The Thom Steele Way dog park is not planned to open in winter because it sits next to a town snow disposal area.

seasonal.title: Summer recreation parking season is over
seasonal.detail: Parking stickers ($5, Conway and Albany full-time residents and second homeowners) are needed at Davis Park, First Bridge, Smith-Eastman, River Road and the resident-only Conway Lake lot from the Saturday of Father's Day weekend to the Sunday of Labor Day weekend. Stickers are sold at the Town Clerk's office. These dates come from the 2024 guidelines.
seasonal.dates: Father's Day weekend to Labor Day weekend

seasonal.title: Winter overnight parking ban starts November 15
seasonal.detail: From November 15 to April 15, no parking on town streets from midnight to 8 a.m. (1:15 a.m. start in some liquor-license areas), and no pushing snow onto streets or sidewalks. Fines are $100 for a first offense and $500 after that.

seasonal.title: Adult pickleball starts November 8
seasonal.detail: Session 1 of town adult pickleball runs November 8 to January 31 with day and evening slots for all levels.

methodology: Compiled October 30, 2026 from pages opened this session: the Conway Parks and Recreation MyRec site (home, facility list and facility pages, staff, programs and calendar), the department's 2024 parking program guidelines, the Town of Conway website (Conservation, Parks and Recreation Areas, Proposed Public Dog Park Project, Public Notices, Town Clerk), Conway town code on eCode360 (Schouler Park), NH State Parks pages for Echo Lake and Cathedral Ledge, the North Conway Community Center MyRec site, and Conway Daily Sun articles (one read through the Laconia Daily Sun). Not covered: the Daily Sun article on the dog park opening and the outcome of the April 2026 rec path ballot article could not be opened; Mount Washington Valley Ski Touring pages and the town trail map PDFs were not opened; the Smith-Eastman area has no official facility page; winter program dates (pond hockey, rink hours) were not yet posted; the department's 2026 parking guidelines were not found, so 2024 rules are shown.
